title: Tenses Quiz 7
description: Every question hides a trap: a false signal word, a participle or a tense that looks right.
instructions: Read each question carefully, then check your answer.
Every question has a trap. Read every word.

questions.question: She said she ___ the letter the day before.
questions.explanation: After said in the past, the earlier action becomes the past perfect. Watch out: the day before points to an action earlier than the saying.

questions.question: 'I have lived here for five years' and 'I have been living here for five years' are both correct.
questions.explanation: Both describe a situation that continues up to now. Watch out: the continuous stresses the duration, but with state verbs such as know, only the simple form is used.

questions.question: He {{1}} (study) for three hours when his friend {{2}} (call).
questions.explanation: A long action before a past moment uses the past perfect continuous, and the later action uses the past simple. Watch out: the studying began before the call.

questions.question: 'I have lost my keys' means...
options: I lost them but found them
I still do not have them
questions.explanation: The present perfect connects the past action to now. Watch out: if I found them, I would say I lost them (past simple).

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: If you finished early, we will leave.
If you finish early, we will leave.
If you finish early, we would leave.
If you will finish early, we will leave.
questions.explanation: After if, the present simple expresses a future condition. Watch out: will is never used in the if clause.

questions.question: Correct the mistake: I am studying English since January.
accepted: I have been studying English since January.
I have been studying English since January
I have studied English since January.
I have studied English since January
questions.explanation: Since + a starting point needs the present perfect or its continuous form. Watch out: the present continuous cannot go with since.

questions.assertion: 'I have visited Rome last year' is incorrect.
questions.reason: The present perfect cannot be used with a finished time such as last year.
questions.explanation: Both are true and the reason explains the mistake: the correct sentence is I visited Rome last year. Watch out: a finished time needs the past simple.

questions.question: This time next week, I {{1}} (lie) on a beach.
questions.explanation: At a particular future time, an action in progress uses will be + -ing. Watch out: lie becomes lying, not lieing.

questions.question: Which sentences are correct?
options: She didn't went to school today.
I have seen that film yesterday.
They had left before we arrived.
questions.explanation: The first two are correct. Watch out: the other two mix a past form with the wrong auxiliary or a finished time.

questions.question: Put the words in the correct order.
questions.explanation: The earlier action, they had gone, is in the past perfect. Watch out: by the time introduces the later action.

questions.question: I haven't seen her ___ Monday.
questions.explanation: Monday is a point in time, so since is used. Watch out: for is used with a length of time.

questions.question: In 'When I was cooking, the phone rang', the phone interrupted the cooking.
questions.explanation: The long action is in the past continuous and the short interrupting action is in the past simple. Watch out: swapping the tenses changes the meaning.
